briefdescription.para: Converts an OpenCV cv::Mat to a 2D Array with optional value scaling to [0, 1].

detaileddescription.para: This function converts an OpenCV cv::Mat object into a 2D Array. The conversion process creates a new Array object and copies the data from the cv::Mat into this Array. If the remap_values parameter is set to true (the default), the values in the resulting Array will be scaled to the interval [0, 1]. If set to false, the values will be copied directly without scaling. Modifications to the Array will not affect the original cv::Mat and vice versa.

memberdef.name: alter_elevation

briefdescription.para: Point-wise alteration: locally enforce a new elevation value while maintaining the 'shape' of the heightmap.

detaileddescription.para: This function modifies the elevation values in the input array based on a cloud of points that specify the coordinates and variations for the alterations. The function ensures that the shape of the heightmap is preserved while applying these local changes.

The alteration is performed using a kernel with a minimal radius (ir) and the intensity of the alterations is scaled based on the footprint_ratio. The shift parameter allows for introducing noise or offset in the alteration process, and the scale parameter is used to adjust the domain of the alteration.

parameterdescription.para: Input array representing the heightmap to be altered. The elevation values in this array will be adjusted according to the cloud data.
Cloud object that defines the coordinates and elevation variations for the alterations. This object provides the necessary data for applying the local changes.
Alteration kernel minimal radius. This parameter defines the minimum size of the kernel used for local alterations.
Defines how the radius of the alteration scales with the variation intensity. A higher ratio results in a larger footprint of the alterations.
Noise shift specified as a vector {xs, ys} for each direction, relative to a unit domain. This allows for adding random offsets to the alteration process.
Domain scaling in the range [0, 1]. This parameter adjusts the domain size over which the alteration is applied.

memberdef.name: base_elevation

briefdescription.para: Generate a heightmap from a coarse grid of control points with defined elevation values.

detaileddescription.para: This function creates a heightmap by interpolating elevation values provided at specific control points on a coarse grid. The result is a finer resolution heightmap where the elevation values are smoothly distributed over the entire grid.

The interpolation is performed using a Gaussian function, with the width_factor parameter controlling the half-width of the base Gaussian function used for smoothing. Optionally, noise can be added using the provided p_noise_x and p_noise_y arrays, and the heightmap can be adjusted by a local wavenumber multiplier specified by p_stretching. The bbox parameter defines the domain bounding box for the heightmap.

parameterdescription.para: Dimensions of the output array (heightmap).
Elevation values at the control points specified on a coarse grid. This 2D vector holds the elevation data at each control point.
Factor applied to the half-width of the Gaussian function used for smoothing the elevations. A value of 1.0 represents the default smoothing width.
Optional pointer to an input noise array affecting the x-direction. If provided, it is used to add noise to the elevation values.
Optional pointer to an input noise array affecting the y-direction. If provided, it is used to add noise to the elevation values.
Optional pointer to an input array that acts as a local wavenumber multiplier. If provided, it adjusts the elevation values according to the local wavenumber.
Domain bounding box specified as a vector {xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax}. This defines the extent of the heightmap in the coordinate space.

simplesect.para: Array A new array representing the generated heightmap with interpolated elevation values.

memberdef.name: elevation_from_sparse_constraints

briefdescription.para: Synthesize a smooth heightmap from sparse elevation constraints using GPU harmonic interpolation (Laplacian PDE).

detaileddescription.para: This function allows generating a continuous terrain elevation model from sparse sketch data by treating the provided constraints as Dirichlet boundary conditions and solving the discrete Laplace equation ($\Delta z = 0$) using GPU-accelerated Red-Black SOR.

parameterdescription.para: Array specifying mountain peak/ridge elevations (> 0).
Optional pointer to coastline mask (fixed to coastline_elevation).
Optional pointer to outer boundary/ocean mask (fixed to boundary_elevation). If null, a 1-pixel boundary border around the domain perimeter is used.
Target elevation scaling for mountains (default: 1.0).
Elevation at coastline (default: 0.0).
Elevation at boundary/ocean (default: -1.0).
Max iterations for GPU solver (default: 500).
Convergence tolerance for early exit (default: 1e-5).
Optional noise array to modulate the free terrain regions.
Amplitude of optional noise detail (default: 0.0).

simplesect.para: Array The resulting smooth synthesized heightmap.

memberdef.name: reverse_midpoint

briefdescription.para: Apply the reverse midpoint displacement algorithm to the input array.

detaileddescription.para: This function implements the reverse midpoint displacement algorithm as described in Belhadj et al. (2005). The algorithm generates a terrain-like structure by applying displacement to the values in the input array based on random noise. The function can be tuned using the seed parameter for random number generation, noise_scale for controlling the amplitude of the noise, and threshold for setting a background value.

parameterdescription.para: Input array to which the reverse midpoint displacement algorithm will be applied. The array's values are modified to produce the output terrain.
Random seed number used to initialize the random number generator for reproducibility.
Amplitude of the noise applied during the displacement process. A higher value results in more pronounced terrain features.
Threshold 'background' value used to influence the displacement algorithm. Values below this threshold may be treated differently depending on the algorithm's design.

simplesect.para: Array The output array after applying the reverse midpoint displacement algorithm. This array contains the modified values representing the generated terrain.

briefdescription.para: Generate a heightmap based on a set of ridgelines and a specified slope.

detaileddescription.para: This function creates a heightmap using a set of ridgelines defined by their x, y, and z coordinates, and applies a specified slope to the ridgelines. The function can optionally apply smoothing, adjust the ridge edge width, and clamp values below a minimum threshold. Additional noise and stretching parameters can be applied to modify the resulting heightmap.

memberdef.name: stamping

briefdescription.para: Generate a heightmap by stamping a kernel at predefined locations.

detaileddescription.para: This function creates a heightmap by stamping a specified kernel at given x, y, and z coordinates. The kernel can be scaled and manipulated based on the z-coordinates of the stamping points, and can be optionally flipped or rotated. The heightmap is generated by blending the results using the specified blending method. Randomization options are available for kernel manipulation.

parameterdescription.para: The dimensions of the output array (heightmap).
A vector of x-coordinates where the kernel is stamped.
A vector of y-coordinates where the kernel is stamped.
A vector of z-coordinates where the kernel is stamped. This affects the kernel radius and amplitude scaling.
The kernel to be stamped onto the heightmap.
The radius of the kernel in pixels.
Boolean flag to scale the kernel radius based on the z-coordinates.
Boolean flag to scale the kernel amplitude based on the z-coordinates.
The method used for blending multiple kernel stamps. Options may include additive, maximum, minimum, etc.
Random seed number for kernel randomization.
Smoothing parameter for the heightmap (e.g., for smooth minimum or maximum blending).
Boolean flag to randomly flip the kernel before stamping. Flipping includes transposing.
Boolean flag to randomly rotate the kernel before stamping. Rotation can be resource-intensive.
Bounding box for the array domain, defining the spatial extent of the heightmap.

simplesect.para: Array The generated heightmap with kernel stamps applied at the specified locations.

memberdef.name: transfer

briefdescription.para: Transfers spatial details from a source array onto a target array.

detaileddescription.para: This function applies a high-pass spatial filter to the source array (using a smoothing pulse of radius ir) to extract its high-frequency content. That content is then scaled by amplitude and blended with the target array. Optionally, the target can be prefiltered before blending.
The result is a new array that combines the base structure of target with the high-frequency details from source.

parameterdescription.para: The input array providing high-frequency details.
The input array providing the base structure.
Radius (in pixels or samples) for the smoothing filter used to separate low/high frequencies.
Scaling factor applied to the high-frequency content extracted from source.
If true, target is smoothed before blending to better integrate with the transferred details.

simplesect.para: A new Array containing the target data enhanced by the source's high-frequency information.

briefdescription.para: Performs linear extrapolation of values at the borders of an array (e.g., i = 0, j = 0, etc.) based on the inner values of the array.

detaileddescription.para: This function modifies the borders of the input array by applying a linear extrapolation method, which uses the values inside the array to estimate and fill in the border values. The extrapolation is influenced by a relaxation coefficient (sigma) and a buffer depth (nbuffer), which determines how many layers of the border are extrapolated.

memberdef.name: coastal_erosion_diffusion

briefdescription.para: Simulates terrain diffusion due to coastal erosion.

detaileddescription.para: This function applies an iterative coastal erosion diffusion process on a terrain elevation array (z), taking into account the presence and depth of water. The erosion model smooths the terrain near shorelines while maintaining constant water-surface height.

At each iteration:
A local water mask is computed using water_mask(water_depth, z, additional_depth).
The terrain elevations are smoothed (diffused) using a masked Laplacian filter, applied only near the water boundary.
The water depth is adjusted to preserve the total water surface height (i.e., z + water_depth remains constant).
This results in a realistic simulation of coastal erosion processes where the terrain near the waterline is progressively smoothed and redistributed.

parameterdescription.para: Reference to the terrain elevation array (modified in place).
Reference to the array representing water depth values (modified to preserve water surface level).
Additional virtual water depth used to estimate the influence region of the shoreline during mask computation.
Number of erosion–diffusion iterations to apply.
Optional output pointer. If non-null, it receives the last computed water mask used during the final iteration.

memberdef.name: coastal_erosion_profile

briefdescription.para: Applies a coastal erosion profile to a terrain elevation field.

detaileddescription.para: This function modifies the elevation array z by carving a coastal profile at the interface between ground and water. It uses distance transforms both from ground regions and from water regions to determine how far each point is from the shoreline. According to this distance, the function applies:

listitem.para: A ground-side shore slope with an optional scarp transition.
A water-side underwater slope ensuring continuity with the ground slope.
An optional post-filtering step (Laplace smoothing) restricted to the shoreline region.

detaileddescription.para: Water depth is adjusted after filtering to preserve the original water surface height.
Optionally, a shoreline mask can be returned describing the region influenced by the coastal transformation.

parameterdescription.para: Array of terrain elevations. Modified in-place.
Array of water depths. Modified to preserve water surface height after terrain changes.
Horizontal extent (in grid units) over which the ground-side shore profile is applied.
Horizontal extent (in grid units) over which the underwater profile is applied.
Ground-side slope magnitude of the coastal profile. Expressed in elevation units per domain width.
Water-side slope magnitude of the underwater profile. Expressed similarly to slope_shore.

Ratio defining the relative extent of the scarp region. A value in [0,1]:
0 → no scarp, only slope
1 → all scarp
If true, applies Laplacian smoothing to z restricted to shoreline areas.
Optional output pointer. If non-null, receives the shoreline mask (values in [0,1]) indicating where the coastal transformation was applied.

memberdef.argsstring: (Array &z, const Array *p_mask, Array &water_depth, float shore_ground_extent, float shore_water_extent, float slope_shore=0.5f, float slope_shore_water=0.5f, float scarp_extent_ratio=0.5f, bool apply_post_filter=true, int post_filter_iterations=3, bool solid_shore_mask=true, float scarp_mask_transition_ratio=0.2f, const Array *p_noise=nullptr, Array *p_shore_mask=nullptr, Array *p_scarp_mask=nullptr)

memberdef.name: hydraulic_stream_upscale_amplification

briefdescription.para: Applies hydraulic erosion with upscaling amplification.

detaileddescription.para: This function progressively upscales the input array z by powers of 2 and applies hydraulic erosion based on flow accumulation at each level of upscaling. After all upscaling levels are processed, the array is resampled back to its original resolution using bilinear interpolation.

parameterdescription.para: Input array representing elevation data.
Erosion coefficient.
Reference talus used to locally define the flow-partition exponent. Smaller values lead to thinner flow streams.
Number of upscaling levels to apply. The function will resample the array at each level.
A scaling factor applied at each level to adjust the impact of the unary operation. Higher persistence values will amplify the effects at each level.
Kernel radius. If ir > 1, a cone kernel is used to carve channel flow erosion.
Flow accumulation clipping ratio.

simplesect.para: The function first applies upscaling using bicubic resampling, performs hydraulic erosion at each level, and finally resamples the array back to its initial resolution using bilinear interpolation.

memberdef.name: export_as_cubemap

briefdescription.para: Exports a 2D array as a cubemap texture with continuity enforcement and overlapping regions.

detaileddescription.para: This function generates a cubemap texture from the input array z, resamples the data to fit the cubemap resolution with optional overlapping regions, and ensures seamless transitions between the six faces of the cubemap. The cubemap can either be saved as a single texture or split into individual face textures.

fname
Output file name or base name for the cubemap files.
z
Input 2D array representing the data to be converted into a cubemap.
cubemap_resolution
Resolution (width and height) of each individual face of the cubemap.
overlap
Fraction (0 to 1) of overlap between adjacent faces to ensure smooth transitions.
ir
Radius parameter for smoothing at triple corners.
cmap
Colormap to be applied when exporting the textures.
splitted
If true, exports each face of the cubemap as a separate image; otherwise, exports the entire cubemap as a single texture.
p_cubemap
Pointer to an optional output array where the final cubemap data will be stored.
The generated cubemap maintains continuity between faces, adjusting values at overlapping regions and corners using smooth transitions. If the splitted flag is set, six individual PNG images are generated for the cubemap faces with appropriate suffixes appended to the base name. Otherwise, the entire cubemap is exported as a single texture file.

briefdescription.para: Enforce a talus slope constraint on a height field.

detaileddescription.para: Cells are processed from highest to lowest using a max-heap. Each cell may raise neighboring cells so that the slope relative to the current cell does not exceed the local talus value.
Intuition: stabilizes an existing terrain by redistributing height so slopes do not exceed the talus limit (similar to talus erosion / relaxation but by adding material).

parameterdescription.para: A reference to the 2D array representing the terrain heights. The function modifies this array in place to introduce talus slopes.

The seed for the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility of the noise effects in the talus formation process. The same seed will produce the same terrain modifications.
A parameter that controls the amount of randomness or noise introduced in the talus formation process. The default value is 0.2.

detaileddescription.para: This function calculates cumulative displacement along the x-axis based on relative elevation differences between adjacent cells. The displacement is scaled and optionally reversed, then used to apply a warping effect to the array, simulating an escarpment feature. An optional global scaling factor can further adjust the displacement effect intensity.

briefdescription.para: Applies a smooth reversal of values above a given threshold.

detaileddescription.para: This function modifies the elements of an array by "reversing" values that exceed a given threshold value, optionally blending the effect over a transition range.

For values above the threshold:
The difference between the value and the threshold is scaled down proportionally to scaling and modulated by a smooth transition (using smoothstep3) based on transition_extent.

For values below the threshold:
The values are linearly blended (lerp) with the threshold value using a smooth transition factor, gradually reducing the reversal effect.

parameterdescription.para: Array to modify in place.
Array containing the per-element threshold values.
Multiplier applied to the difference above the threshold.
Width of the smooth transition zone for blending.

briefdescription.para: Smooth the path using B-Spline curves.

detaileddescription.para: This method smooths the path using B-Spline curves, which provide a smooth curve that passes through the control points. The edge_divisions parameter defines the number of subdivisions per edge for achieving smooth curves.

Important: This function does not correctly handle closed polylines (circular contours). If the path is closed, the smoothing may not correctly close the loop, potentially leaving a gap between the start and end points.

edge_divisions
Number of subdivisions per edge to achieve a smooth B-Spline curve.
This function does not correctly handle closed polylines.
edm
Mode for dividing edges. Default is EDM_PER_EDGE.
See unit tests: test_splines.cpp

briefdescription.para: Smooth the path using Catmull-Rom curves.

detaileddescription.para: This method applies Catmull-Rom curve smoothing to the path. Catmull-Rom splines are interpolating splines that pass through each control point. The edge_divisions parameter determines the number of subdivisions per edge for smoothing.

parameterdescription.para: Number of edge subdivisions to create a smooth Catmull-Rom curve.
Mode for dividing edges. Default is EDM_PER_EDGE.

detaileddescription.para: See unit tests: test_splines.cpp

briefdescription.para: Smooth the path using De Casteljau curves.

detaileddescription.para: This function smooths a path by applying De Casteljau's algorithm to generate intermediate points along the path, effectively creating a Bézier curve that approximates the original path. The path is divided into segments, and the De Casteljau algorithm is applied to each segment, resulting in a smooth curve.

The parameter edge_divisions controls the number of divisions (sub-segments) created along each segment of the path. A higher number of divisions will result in a smoother curve, but will also increase the computational cost.

parameterdescription.para: The number of divisions for each edge of the path. Default is 10, which provides a balanced level of smoothing.
Mode for dividing edges (default is EDM_PER_EDGE).

detaileddescription.para: See unit tests: test_splines.cpp

briefdescription.para: Simplifies the current path using the Visvalingam-Whyatt algorithm.

parameterdescription.para: The input path to be decimated.

The desired number of points to retain in the path. If the current number of points is less than n_points_target or the path contains fewer than 3 points, the method returns without modifying the path.

detaileddescription.para: See unit tests: test_decimate_vw.cpp

memberdef.name: smooth

briefdescription.para: Applies a smoothing operation to the path points using a moving average filter.

detaileddescription.para: This method smooths the path points based on a specified number of neighboring points, an averaging intensity, and an inertia factor. The smoothing involves calculating the average of neighboring points within a range defined by navg, and then applying an intensity-based weighted average to blend the original and smoothed values. Additionally, an inertia effect can be applied to gradually adjust point positions based on previous points.

parameterdescription.para: The input path to be smoothed.
Number of neighboring points to consider on each side of the current point during the smoothing process. Higher values result in broader smoothing.
The weight given to the averaged points. A value of 1.0 applies full intensity, resulting in a complete averaging of the neighboring points. Lower values retain more of the original point's position.

The factor by which each point is influenced by its previous point after the initial smoothing pass. A value of 0 has no inertia effect, while a higher value blends the current point's position with that of the preceding point, creating a trailing effect.

briefdescription.para: Compute the divergence of a 2D gradient field.

detaileddescription.para: Given two scalar fields representing the horizontal and vertical derivatives of a height map: \[ p(x, y) = \frac{\partial h}{\partial x}, \qquad q(x, y) = \frac{\partial h}{\partial y} \] this function returns the divergence: \[ f(x, y) = \frac{\partial p}{\partial x}(x, y) + \frac{\partial q}{\partial y}(x, y) \]
The divergence is a key term for solving the Poisson equation $\nabla^2 h = f$ when reconstructing a height field from gradients or from a normal map.

dx
Array of horizontal derivatives ( $\partial h / \partial x$). Must have the same dimensions as dy.
dy
Array of vertical derivatives ( $\partial h / \partial y$). Must have the same dimensions as dx.
A new Array containing the divergence $f(x, y)$ for each pixel. The returned array has the same size as the inputs.
See unit tests: test_gradient.cpp

briefdescription.para: Computes a smoothed gradient angle (aspect) field with circular unwrapping.

The angle field is smoothed by converting the angle to a unit vector representation on the circle, applying a local smoothing kernel, and converting it back to an angle. This results in a continuous aspect map that is ideal for visualization or further processing.

listitem.para: Regions with very low gradient magnitude may produce unstable angle values; these regions should typically be masked or treated separately.

briefdescription.para: Solve the Poisson equation ∇²h = rhs using Gauss–Seidel iteration.

detaileddescription.para: This function assumes Dirichlet boundary conditions (height = 0 at the edges). The algorithm updates interior points according to: \[ h(x, y) = (1 - \omega) h(x, y) + \omega \cdot 0.25 \big( h(x+1, y) + h(x-1, y) + h(x, y+1) + h(x, y-1) - rhs(x, y) \big) \]

memberdef.name: flow_accumulation_stochastic

briefdescription.para: Computes flow accumulation using a stochastic (Monte-Carlo) transport estimator.

detaileddescription.para: Particles are spawned uniformly, advected along the downhill gradient field with exact voxel traversal, attenuated by an optional decay term, and deposit flux into every cell they exit. A final analytic normalization yields the steady-state flux, including for cells no particle visited. Compared to flow_accumulation_d8, the result is smooth and free of axis-aligned artifacts.
Port of the reference implementation of "Stochastic Geomorphological Transport for Terrain Erosion Simulation" (N. McDonald, G. Cordonnier), https://github.com/erosiv/geotransport (MIT).
Results are reproducible up to floating-point summation order (deposits accumulate via unordered atomic adds).

parameterdescription.para: Input array representing the heightmap values.
Number of Monte-Carlo samples (particles).
Random seed number (deterministic for fixed inputs).
Optional per-cell source term (default: uniform 1).
Optional per-cell decay rate (default: 0, pure accumulation).

simplesect.para: Array Per-cell steady-state flux.

The flow-partition exponent is locally defined using a reference talus value, where smaller values of talus_ref will lead to narrower flow streams. The maximum talus value of the heightmap can be used as a reference.

parameterdescription.para: Input array representing the heightmap values.

briefdescription.para: Simulates a local increase in water depth without global reflooding.

detaileddescription.para: This function propagates an additional water depth over a terrain elevation map (z), starting only from cells that already contain water in the input water_depth array. The propagation is restricted to neighboring cells of higher elevation (8-connectivity), preventing the formation of entirely new flooded basins disconnected from the original water region.

Unlike water_depth_increase_with_flooding(), this function does not perform a full flooding simulation of the domain. It is primarily intended for expanding or softening an existing water mask slightly beyond the current shoreline.

parameterdescription.para: Input array representing the initial water depth.
Elevation array corresponding to the same grid as water_depth.
Additional water depth to propagate from the existing water region.

simplesect.para: An Array containing the updated water depth after local propagation.
Water spreads only upward toward neighboring cells with higher elevation. Existing disconnected dry basins are not flooded.
This function is useful for generating extended shoreline masks, erosion influence regions, or visually expanding water boundaries without performing a physically complete flooding simulation.

briefdescription.para: Simulates a physical rise in water level with full domain flooding.

detaileddescription.para: This function increases the water level by additional_depth and recomputes flooding over the terrain elevation map (z). Unlike water_depth_increase(), the propagation is not restricted to the vicinity of the original water region: water may spread through connected terrain and flood previously dry areas if they become reachable under the new water level.

The simulation behaves more like a physical flooding process where rising water can overflow barriers, connect basins, and eventually inundate large portions of the domain depending on terrain topology.

parameterdescription.para: Input array representing the initial water depth.
Elevation array corresponding to the same grid as water_depth.
Additional water depth used to raise the global water level.

simplesect.para: An Array containing the updated flooded state after recomputing water propagation.
Flood propagation may extend far beyond the original water mask and can potentially inundate the entire connected terrain domain.
This function is more physically plausible than water_depth_increase(), and is suitable for terrain flooding simulations, overflow analysis, or hydrological studies.

briefdescription.para: Perform harmonic interpolation on a 2D array using the Successive Over-Relaxation (SOR) method.

detaileddescription.para: This function solves the discrete Laplace equation on a regular grid by iteratively updating the values of an input array. Values marked as fixed in the mask_fixed_values remain unchanged throughout the process. The algorithm stops when either the maximum number of iterations is reached or the change between successive iterations falls below the specified tolerance.

Mask of the same shape as array. Cells with a value greater than zero indicate fixed points that must remain unchanged during interpolation.

Convergence criterion: the algorithm stops if the maximum absolute update between iterations is less than this value.
Relaxation factor (1 < omega < 2 recommended). Values closer to 2 accelerate convergence, but overly large values may cause divergence.

simplesect.para: A new 2D array containing the interpolated solution.

listitem.para: The algorithm updates only the interior points (indices [1..nx-2, 1..ny-2]).
Cells where mask_fixed_values(i, j) > 0 remain unchanged.
A relaxation factor of 1 corresponds to the standard Jacobi/Gauss-Seidel update.

memberdef.name: harmonic_interpolation

briefdescription.para: Perform harmonic interpolation on a 2D array with 2D variable diffusion coefficients (Dx, Dy) using the Successive Over-Relaxation (SOR) method.

detaileddescription.para: Solves the steady-state anisotropic diffusion equation: \[ \nabla \cdot (\mathbf{D} \nabla u) = \frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(D_x \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}\right) + \frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(D_y \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}\right) = 0 \]

parameterdescription.para: Input 2D array providing the initial guess.
Mask where values > 0 indicate fixed boundary constraints.
Array of diffusion coefficients in the x-direction.
Array of diffusion coefficients in the y-direction.
Maximum number of SOR iterations.
Convergence tolerance.
Relaxation factor (0 = auto-computed optimal).

simplesect.para: Interpolated array.

briefdescription.para: Generates a disk-shaped kernel footprint.

detaileddescription.para: This function creates a disk-shaped kernel, which is a circular kernel where the values are radially symmetric around the center.

parameterdescription.para: Array shape specifying the dimensions of the kernel.

simplesect.para: Array A new array containing the disk-shaped kernel.

briefdescription.para: Generates a smooth, disk-shaped kernel footprint with soft edges.

detaileddescription.para: This function creates a 2D, disk-shaped kernel with radially symmetric values centered in the array. Values inside the cutoff radius r_cutoff are set to 1.0. Between r_cutoff and the normalized radius 1.0, the values smoothly fall off to zero using a parabolic profile to ensure soft transitions at the disk boundary.
The generated array is useful for constructing smooth low-pass filters or spatial masks with circular support.

parameterdescription.para: The dimensions of the output array (width, height).
Normalized cutoff radius in the range [0.0, 1.0]. Inside this radius, the kernel has a flat value of 1.0; outside, it decays smoothly to 0.0.

simplesect.para: A 2D array of size shape containing the smooth disk-shaped kernel.
Coordinates are normalized such that the radius 1.0 corresponds to the maximum possible distance from the center in either dimension.

briefdescription.para: Computes the downstream path length to the domain outlet.

simplesect.para: Array Resulting array containing the local maxima.

briefdescription.para: Computes the local median deviation of a 2D array.

detaileddescription.para: This function calculates the absolute difference between the local mean and a pseudo-local median of each element in the input array. The local neighborhood is defined by a square window with radius ir.

parameterdescription.para: The input 2D array of values (e.g., a heightmap).
The radius of the square neighborhood window used for computing local statistics. The window size is (2*ir + 1) x (2*ir + 1).

simplesect.para: A new array of the same size as array, where each element represents the absolute deviation between the local mean and pseudo-local median in its neighborhood.
The function uses a pseudo-median approximation. For exact median computation, replace the median_pseudo() call with a proper median filter implementation.
local_mean(), median_pseudo()

briefdescription.para: Return the local minima based on a maximum filter with a square kernel.

parameterdescription.para: Input array from which local minima are to be extracted.

simplesect.para: Array Resulting array containing the local minima.

briefdescription.para: Return the local mean based on a mean filter with a square kernel.

detaileddescription.para: This function calculates the local mean of the input array using a mean filter with a square kernel. The local mean is determined by averaging values within a square neighborhood defined by the footprint radius ir. The result is an array where each value represents the mean of the surrounding values within the kernel size.

parameterdescription.para: Input array from which the local mean is to be calculated.
Square kernel footprint radius. The size of the kernel used to compute the local mean.

simplesect.para: Array Resulting array containing the local means.

briefdescription.para: Calculates the relative elevation within a specified radius, helping to identify local highs and lows.

detaileddescription.para: Relative elevation analysis determines how high or low a point is relative to its surroundings, which can be critical in hydrological modeling and geomorphology.

Usage:
Use this function to detect local depressions or peaks in the terrain, which could indicate potential water collection points or hilltops.
Useful in flood risk assessment and landscape classification.

parameterdescription.para: The input array representing the terrain elevation data.
The radius (in pixels) within which to calculate the relative elevation for each point.

simplesect.para: Array An output array containing the relative elevation values, normalized between 0 and 1.

briefdescription.para: Computes the ruggedness of each element in the input array.

detaileddescription.para: The ruggedness is calculated as the square root of the sum of squared differences between each element and its neighbors within a specified radius.

parameterdescription.para: The input array for which ruggedness is to be computed.
The radius within which neighbors are considered for ruggedness calculation.

simplesect.para: An array containing the ruggedness values for each element in the input array.

briefdescription.para: Estimates the rugosity of a surface by analyzing the skewness of the elevation data, which reflects surface roughness.

detaileddescription.para: Rugosity is a measure of terrain roughness, often used in ecological studies and habitat mapping. Higher rugosity values indicate more rugged terrain, which can affect species distribution and water flow.

parameterdescription.para: The input array representing the heightmap data (elevation values).
The radius of the square kernel used for calculations, determining the scale of the analysis.
Return the convex rugosity if true, and the concave ones if not.

simplesect.para: Array An output array containing the rugosity estimates, where higher values indicate rougher terrain.

briefdescription.para: Measures the valley width by calculating the distance from each point in a concave region to the frontier of that region.

detaileddescription.para: Valley width is a geomorphological metric that represents the distance across valleys or concave regions in a terrain. This measurement is particularly useful in hydrological modeling and landscape analysis, where valley dimensions are important.

listitem.para: Use this function to assess the width of valleys within a terrain, which can be important for understanding water flow, sediment transport, and landform development.
Applicable in studies focusing on river valleys, canyon analysis, and erosion patterns.

parameterdescription.para: The input array representing the heightmap data (elevation values).
The radius used for pre-filtering, controlling the scale of analysis (in pixels). The default value is 0, meaning no pre-filtering is applied.
If enabled, selects ridges instead of valleys.

simplesect.para: Array An output array containing valley width values, representing the distance to the edge of the concave region for each point.

briefdescription.para: Computes the relative distance of each non-zero cell in a binary array from the skeleton and border.

detaileddescription.para: This function calculates a relative distance measure for each non-zero cell in the input array. The measure is defined as the ratio of the cell's distance to the nearest border and the combined distances to the nearest skeleton and border cells. The skeleton is computed using the Zhang-Suen skeletonization algorithm.

If true, the borders of the skeletonized image will be set to zero.

simplesect.para: An array representing the relative distance map, where each cell has a value between 0 and 1. A value closer to 1 indicates proximity to the skeleton, while a value closer to 0 indicates proximity to the border.
The skeleton is computed using the Zhang-Suen skeletonization algorithm.

memberdef.name: downscale_transform

briefdescription.para: Applies a downscaling transformation to a 2D array using Fourier-based filtering.

detaileddescription.para: This function performs a series of operations on a 2D array to isolate and transform its low-frequency components. It uses a Fourier transform for filtering, downscales the array for efficient processing, applies a user-defined unary operation, and then restores the transformed low-frequency content to the original resolution.

parameterdescription.para: A reference to the input 2D array to be transformed. The array may be resized internally.
The cutoff wavenumber for isolating low-frequency components during filtering.
A user-defined function that applies a transformation to the downscaled array.

listitem.para: The function ensures that the input array is square for Fourier operations by resampling it if necessary.
A smooth low-pass filter is applied in the frequency domain, and the filtered array is downscaled to a coarse resolution.
The user-defined transformation (unary_op) is applied to the downscaled array.
The transformed low-frequency content is upsampled and reintegrated into the original array.
If the input array was not square, the final result is resampled back to its original shape.

detaileddescription.para: This function progressively upscales the given array by powers of 2 (starting from the initial shape), performs a user-defined unary operation on the upscaled array at each level, and finally returns the array to its original resolution using bilinear interpolation.

The number of upscaling levels to apply. The function will resample the array for each level.

simplesect.para: The function first applies bicubic resampling to upscale the array, then applies the user-provided unary_op at each upscaling level. After all levels are processed, the array is resampled back to its initial shape using bilinear interpolation.

memberdef.name: diffusion_limited_aggregation

briefdescription.para: Generates a diffusion-limited aggregation (DLA) pattern.

detaileddescription.para: This function simulates the diffusion-limited aggregation process to generate a pattern within a grid of specified dimensions. The DLA process models particles that undergo a random walk until they stick to a seed, gradually forming complex fractal structures.

parameterdescription.para: The dimensions of the grid where the DLA pattern will be generated. It is represented as a glm::ivec2 object, where the first element is the width and the second element is the height.
A scaling factor that influences the density of the particles in the DLA pattern.
The radius within which initial seeding of particles occurs. This radius defines the area where the first particles are placed.
The ratio between the outer seeding radius and the initial seeding radius. It determines the outer boundary for particle seeding.
Slope of the talus added to the DLA pattern.
A parameter that controls the amount of randomness or noise introduced in the talus formation process.
The seed for the random number generator, ensuring reproducibility of the pattern. The same seed will generate the same pattern.

simplesect.para: A 2D array representing the generated DLA pattern. The array is of the same size as specified by shape.

memberdef.name: bump_lorentzian

briefdescription.para: Generates a 2D Lorentzian bump pattern.

detaileddescription.para: This function fills an array with values computed from a normalized Lorentzian-shaped bump function. The bump is centered at a given position, has a specified radius, and can vary in width depending on a control parameter. Optional noise arrays can be applied to perturb the x and y coordinates before evaluation.
The Lorentzian function is normalized so that it returns 1.0 at the center and smoothly decays to 0.0 at the radius boundary. Outside the radius, the value is exactly 0.

parameterdescription.para: Dimensions of the output array (width, height).
Scaling factor controlling the bump width relative to the control parameter.
Radius of the bump in the coordinate space of bbox.
Optional pointer to an array of per-pixel control parameters. If provided, it modulates the width of the Lorentzian bump.
Optional pointer to an array of x-offset noise values. Values are added to the x coordinate before evaluation.
Optional pointer to an array of y-offset noise values. Values are added to the y coordinate before evaluation.
Center of the bump in the coordinate space of bbox.
Bounding box (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) defining the coordinate space for the array.

simplesect.para: A new Array object of size shape containing the bump pattern.
The function normalizes the Lorentzian curve so that the maximum value is 1 at the center and smoothly decays to 0 at the boundary defined by radius.

memberdef.name: island_chain_land_mask

briefdescription.para: Generates a land mask of an island chain scattered along a path.

detaileddescription.para: Spawns island_count islands along the input path. Each island is an fbm-perturbed radial blob (same construction as island_land_mask). Island positions follow the path arc length, optionally jittered along and across the path by scatter. Island sizes follow a signed falloff: size_falloff = 0 gives uniform sizes, +1 shrinks the islands toward the path end (hotspot-chain look, largest island at the head), -1 shrinks them toward the start; size_jitter adds per-island random variation.

ClampMode::NEGATIVE_ONLY Keeps only negative values, reverses their sign (making them positive), and clamps them to a maximum value vmax. Positive values are set to 0.
ClampMode::BOTH Keeps both positive and negative values, clamping them symmetrically between -vmax and vmax.

memberdef.name: dijkstra

briefdescription.para: Divide the path by adding points based on the lowest elevation difference between each pair of edge endpoints.

detaileddescription.para: This method uses the elevation map to subdivide the path by adding intermediate points where the elevation difference between edges is minimal. The elevation_ratio parameter balances the influence of absolute elevation versus elevation difference in the cost function used for path finding. The distance_exponent affects the weight function used in Dijkstra's algorithm. Areas defined by the p_mask_nogo mask are avoided.

parameterdescription.para: Elevation map used to determine elevation differences along the path.
Bounding box of the domain, defining the area where elevation data is valid.

memberdef.name: quilting

detaileddescription.para: This function creates a new heightmap by stitching patches from a set of input heightmaps. Allow transposition of patches (for square patches).

memberdef.name: translate

briefdescription.para: Translates a 2D array by a specified amount along the x and y axes.

detaileddescription.para: This function shifts the contents of the input array by dx and dy units along the x and y axes, respectively. It supports both periodic boundary conditions, where the array wraps around, and non-periodic conditions, where the shifted areas are filled with zeros.

parameterdescription.para: The input 2D array to be translated. This array remains unmodified.
The translation distance along the x-axis. Positive values shift the array to the right.
The translation distance along the y-axis. Positive values shift the array downward.

If set to true, the translation is periodic, meaning that elements that move out of one side of the array reappear on the opposite side. If false, the areas exposed by the translation are filled with zeros. The default is false.
Optional pointer to a 2D array that contains x-direction noise to be added to the translation. If provided, the noise values are added to dx on a per-element basis.
Optional pointer to a 2D array that contains y-direction noise to be added to the translation. If provided, the noise values are added to dy on a per-element basis.
Domain bounding box.

simplesect.para: A new 2D array that is the result of translating the input array by the specified dx and dy values.

memberdef.name: zoom

briefdescription.para: Applies a zoom effect to a 2D array with an adjustable center.

detaileddescription.para: This function scales the input 2D array by a specified zoom factor, effectively resizing the array's contents. The zoom operation is centered around a specified point within the array, allowing for flexible zooming behavior. The function supports both periodic boundary conditions, where the array wraps around, and non-periodic conditions, where areas outside the original array bounds are filled with zeros.

parameterdescription.para: The input 2D array to be zoomed. This array remains unmodified.
The factor by which to zoom the array. A value greater than 1 enlarges the contents, while a value between 0 and 1 reduces them.

If set to true, the zoom is periodic, meaning that elements moving out of the array bounds due to the zoom reappear on the opposite side. If false, areas outside the original array bounds are filled with zeros. The default is false.
The center of the zoom operation, specified as a glm::vec2 with coordinates in the range [0, 1], where {0.5f, 0.5f} represents the center of the array. The default center is {0.5f, 0.5f}.

Optional pointer to a 2D array that contains x-direction noise to be added during the zoom operation. If provided, the noise values are applied to the x-coordinates of the zoomed array on a per-element basis.

Optional pointer to a 2D array that contains y-direction noise to be added during the zoom operation. If provided, the noise values are applied to the y-coordinates of the zoomed array on a per-element basis.
Domain bounding box.

simplesect.para: A new 2D array that is the result of applying the zoom effect to the input array by the specified zoom_factor and centered at the specified center.
